title: ASR Fetch Record (fetches.jsonl line and .fetch.json sidecar)
description: One exercised recipe: real data pulled through a profiled endpoint. The same object is appended to the source's tracked fetches.jsonl AND written beside the payload as <payload>.fetch.json — so the registry remembers every exercised recipe even after gitignored payloads are cleaned up. The retrieval block is field-compatible with UPC source.retrieval by construction (crosswalks/upc.md): a fetched payload can seed a UPC source without translation. Recorded URLs and params are secret-redacted; the payload itself is whatever the source returned.

url.description: Fully substituted request URL, credential value replaced by *** BEFORE recording.

retrieval.description: UPC-compatible retrieval block. Field names and the fetch_status enum match UPC source.retrieval exactly, so this block can be copied into a UPC source verbatim.

original_url.description: The requested URL (redacted) — maps to UPC retrieval.original_url.

fetch_method.description: Always "http" for the reference CLI; a rendering harness writes its own value.

sha256.description: Hash of the complete payload bytes as stored; null when nothing was stored.

payload.description: Where the full payload landed (gitignored fetched/); the file may be cleaned up later — sha256/bytes in retrieval remain the durable record. null when the fetch was refused or skipped.

pages.description: Number of pages concatenated/collected when pagination ran; null for single requests.

sample.description: Present when --keep-sample stored a truncated, TRACKED sample under the source's samples/ directory (cap recorded in truncated_at; hash is of the stored sample bytes).

truncated_at.description: Byte cap applied; null when the sample is the complete payload.

skip_reason.description: Human-readable reason when the fetch did not execute (credential unresolved with the tried chain listed, robots disallowed, budget exhausted). A skipped fetch is a successful CLI run (exit 0) that honestly did nothing.
